text: In a dispersive medium, which statement correctly distinguishes phase velocity from group velocity?
choices: Phase velocity v_p = ω/k is the speed of a surface of constant phase; group velocity v_g = dω/dk is the speed of energy and information transport
Phase velocity is dω/dk, while group velocity is ω/k
They are always equal, even in a dispersive medium
The group velocity is always greater than c in any medium
explanation: By definition v_p = ω/k (constant-phase surface) and v_g = dω/dk (envelope, energy, and information). Choice 1 swaps the two formulas; choice 2 is false because dispersion (n depending on ω) makes them differ; and while v_p can exceed c near a resonance, v_g being always > c is not generally true.
